sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Ocean Township, NJ?
sections.html:
Ocean Township sits in east central Monmouth County, and a sale there needs a Code Compliance Inspection Certificate from the township's Housing Division before anyone moves in. You can list the house, sell it yourself or accept a cash offer, but the township inspection applies to each of them.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 28,088 residents across 10.87 square miles of land, compared with 27,672 at the 2020 census. Many sellers searching for Ocean mean this Monmouth County township, which is separate from Ocean Township in Ocean County. The township has no downtown. Its homes are spread over three main communities, Oakhurst, Wanamassa and Wayside, so a house is usually described by neighborhood.

sections.h2: How is Ocean Township laid out, and where do the neighborhoods sit?
sections.html:
The Legislature created the township on February 21, 1849 from part of Shrewsbury Township, and later carved off Long Branch, Asbury Park, Deal, Allenhurst and several other shore towns. What remained is a township that borders Eatontown and West Long Branch to the north, Long Branch, Deal, Allenhurst and Interlaken to the east, Neptune and Asbury Park to the south and Tinton Falls to the west.

Two ZIP codes cover most of it: 07755 for Oakhurst and 07712 for Wanamassa and Wayside. Deal Lake, a 158-acre lake shared by seven municipalities with about 27 miles of shoreline, forms part of the eastern edge and is overseen by the Deal Lake Commission, created in 1974. If your house is close to the lake, expect buyers to ask about basement moisture, and expect the inspector to look for signs of leaks and cellar water.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Ocean Township homes?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home is worth $678,300 for 2020 through 2024, and 62.7 percent of households own. About one in five residents is 65 or older, and 90.9 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, so many homes change hands rarely and may need updating.

sections.h2: What does the Ocean Township code compliance inspection involve?
sections.html:
The Housing Division inspects every sale and every rental that changes occupancy. The township's page states that all sale permits must be closed before the inspection is called, no new occupant may move in before the certificate is issued, and post-dated checks are returned. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The checklist is a visual inspection:

  • Exterior: peeling paint, gutters and leaders, doors, windows and screens, siding, sheds and fences, trash and weeds.
  • House number at least 3 inches high and visible from the street.
  • A handrail where stairs have more than four risers, and a guardrail where an open porch or landing is more than 30 inches high.
  • Interior: plumbing in the kitchen and baths, ceilings and walls, signs of leaks or cellar water, enough outlets with covers, locks and ventilation.
  • A pressure and temperature valve with an extension pipe on the water heater.
  • A tip-over bracket on any stove made after 1991.

All utilities must be on at the time of inspection, and a home on a well needs a certified lab report meeting New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection standards. The township's housing forms page also carries a lead paint information sheet.

sections.h2: Who handles smoke and carbon monoxide certificates in Ocean Township?
sections.html:
The Fire District forms are separate from the Housing Division's inspection. Ocean Township has Fire District No. 1 and No. 2, and the township's forms page links an online smoke detector, carbon monoxide and fire extinguisher application for each. Ask the district that covers your street which one applies.

The state Division of Fire Safety says a certificate of smoke alarm compliance is required before a one- or two-family home is sold, that it comes through the municipality, and that it is valid for six months. Time the fire inspection so the certificate still covers your closing date.

sections.h2: What state costs and deadlines apply to an Ocean Township sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the Realty Transfer Fee at recording. The state's own example shows $1,910 on a $325,000 deed with no exemption, and a qualifying senior seller on a $280,000 deed pays $475. The extra 1 percent buyer fee applies only above $1,000,000, which is outside the range of most Ocean Township sales given the $678,300 median.

A Gross Income Tax form must accompany the deed. New Jersey residents sign the GIT/REP-3, and nonresident owners use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless they qualify for an assurance.

Monmouth County follows a different appeal calendar from most of the state. The Division of Taxation's Form A-1 says appeals filed with the Monmouth County Tax Board must be received by January 15, or 45 days after the bulk mailing of assessment notices, whichever is later. A missed deadline means the appeal is dismissed for lateness, so check the date early in the year.

sections.h2: How do roads, trains and schools affect Ocean Township buyers?
sections.html:
Route 18 crosses the western part of the township and Route 35 the east. Route 66 forms the southern border with Neptune, and Route 71 follows the eastern line with Deal, West Long Branch and Long Branch. The Garden State Parkway is just west in Tinton Falls. Shopping clusters on those corridors, including Ocean Commons on Route 35 and Seaview Shopping Center off Route 66.

The North Jersey Coast Line runs through a short stretch of the east side, but the closest stations are at Allenhurst and Elberon. NJ Transit buses 832 and 837 serve the township, and the SeaStreak ferry from Highlands is a 25 to 30 minute drive away.

The Ocean Township School District has five schools and 3,263 students for 2023-24: Ocean Township Elementary in Oakhurst, Wanamassa Elementary, Wayside Elementary, the Intermediate School for grades 5 to 8 and Ocean Township High School. Buyers often ask which elementary school serves an address, so have that answer ready.

sections.h2: When is a cash offer a reasonable option for an Ocean Township house?
sections.html:
Cash is worth pricing when a house fails the code checklist and you do not want to pay for repairs, when you inherited it, or when you need a firm closing date. Ask the buyer to state in writing who orders the Housing Division inspection and who pays for corrections.

Rental owners should also know the township asks landlords to register and pay before March 1 each year. If a rental house is being sold, settle with the tenant and buyer how the occupancy change is handled.

faqs.q: Is there a township inspection before I can sell in Ocean Township?
faqs.a: Yes. The Housing Division performs a code compliance inspection on every sale and on rentals that change occupancy. All sale permits must be closed before the inspection is requested, and nobody may occupy the house until the certificate is issued.

faqs.q: What does the Ocean Township inspection checklist look like?
faqs.a: It is a visual inspection of the exterior and interior. It covers peeling paint, gutters, a 3-inch house number, handrails past four risers, plumbing, leaks, outlets with covers, a water heater valve with an extension pipe and a stove tip-over bracket on models made after 1991.

faqs.q: When is the property tax appeal deadline in Monmouth County?
faqs.a: January 15, or 45 days after the bulk mailing of assessment notices if that is later. The state's Form A-1 singles out Monmouth, Burlington and Gloucester counties for this earlier date, while most other counties use April 1.

faqs.q: How long does a smoke alarm certificate last?
faqs.a: Six months from issue. The Division of Fire Safety requires it before a one- or two-family home is sold, and the owner obtains it through the municipality. In Ocean Township the fire districts provide the application forms.

faqs.q: Do I owe the New Jersey buyer 1 percent fee when I sell?
faqs.a: No. The 1 percent fee is paid by the buyer, and only when total consideration exceeds $1,000,000. Sellers pay the standard Realty Transfer Fee, which depends on the price stated in the deed and any exemption claimed.
